1) motor cortex stimulation (MCS) is an effective treatment for neuropathic pain, 2) corollary discharging is a possible mechanism of MCS and, 3) the right dorsolaterl prefrontal cortex is an interesting target for neuromodulation of chronic pain.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the motor cortex is a potential target for neuromodulation of pain, but its role is probably not as straightforward as previously thought and that the role of corollary discharge is likely to be more important than previously assumed.

motor cortex stimulation might not only have an analgesic action by modulating pain transmission but it could also have an important role in restoring normal corollary discharge activity, which might be altered in chronic pain conditions.

motor cortex stimulation might have a beneficial effect in chronic pain by enhancing corollary discharging from the motor cortex, or by enhancing the processing of such discharges in the right DLPC, or both.
